newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian "large farm' grain crop totals 58.5 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Russian "large farm' grain crop totals 58.5 mln T.

text.p: Russia had threshed 58.5 million tonnes bunker weight of grain by September 21, three million tonnes more than at this time last year, Interfax news agency quoted a senior agriculture official as saying on Tuesday.
Ivan Gridasov, head of the ministry's crop-growing department, said grain yields were 1.65 tonnes per hectare against 1.46 tonnes in 1995.

Gridasov's figure for the net harvest so far was below the 63 million tonnes bunker weight that he reported to Interfax on September 19. A State Statistics Committee spokesman said the 58.5 millions figure did not include output by small, private farmers.
Gridasov declined to comment on the discrepancy, saying that Russian harvest figures were a state secret.
Western Siberia, hit by rainy weather and a lack of threshing equipment, had harvested only 39 percent of its grain crops --- half as much as year-ago levels.

Gridasov said 9.3 million hectares of grain remained to be harvested across Russia, including 7.7 million in Siberia and the Urals regions. Thirty four percent of sown acreage in Eastern Siberia and 58 percent of crops in the Sverdlovsk Urals region had been brought in.
Gridasov was quoted as saying Russia had sown 9.7 million hectares to winter grains, 1.8 million hectares less than at this time last year. --Peter Henderson, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
